text: Acruvium () was founded or first settled around 330 BCE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Kotor: 'Wikipedia's infobox gives the founding as the 5th century BC, but its text says the exact time of foundation of the first settlement is not known; first mentioned in 168 BC.'
fix: Change to 'before the 2nd century BCE (first mentioned 168 BCE; infobox says 5th century BCE)'. No source gives 330 BCE.

text: Diano Marina () was founded or first settled around 30 BCE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Diano Marina: 'The settlement took the name Lucus Bormani... and reached its peak when the Via Iulia Augusta opened (13-12 B.C.)'
fix: 13-12 BCE is when the Roman roadside settlement peaked, not when it was founded. Another guide gives about 200 BCE for the Roman settlement. Reword or change the date.

text: Serra Orrios () was founded or first settled around 2000 BCE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Nuragic complex of Serra Orrios: 'The village's life began in the late Bronze Age (16th century BC) and ended in the Iron Age (9th to 6th century BC).'
source: Wikipedia, Nuragic complex of Serra Orrios
fix: Use about 1550 BCE (2nd millennium BCE). 2000 BCE is too early.

text: Capo Testa () was founded or first settled around 330 BCE (approx.).
evidence: Capo Testa, Cala Grande, Valle della Luna, Santa Teresa di Gallura (SS) (idese.cultura.gov.it): 'The excavations carried out at Capo Testa have documented two phases of Roman attendance. The first dates back to the end of the Republican Age and the first imperial age.'
source: Capo Testa, Cala Grande, Valle della Luna, Santa Teresa di Gallura (SS) (idese.cultura.gov.it)
fix: The documented Roman quarrying and settlement begin in the 1st century BCE, not 330 BCE. Change the date or drop the claim.

text: Histria () was founded or first settled around 550 BCE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Histria (ancient city): 'Founded by settlers from Miletus in the 7th century BCE; 657 BC according to Eusebius, or perhaps a little later.'
fix: Change to about 657 BCE (mid-7th century BCE), not 550 BCE.

text: Alea ended or was abandoned around 300 CE.
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source found for abandonment around 300 CE. Pausanias (2nd century CE) still describes temples there. The Tegea-related Alea was destroyed by the Goths in 395 CE.

text: Van vilayet ended or was abandoned around 1922 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Van vilayet: 'Wikipedia's infobox lists the Van Vilayet as disestablished in 1922, with Turkey as its successor.'

text: Torre Alocaz ended or was abandoned around 640 CE.
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source gives an abandonment date of about 640 CE. The place is a pedanía of Utrera, still inhabited, and a medieval village (Aloquaz) under Alfonso X.

text: Polizzello archaeological site ended or was abandoned around 550 BCE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Polizzello archaeological site: 'inhabited probably from the eleventh to the sixth century BC'

text: Palenque: Maya city of Pakal the Great, with superb inscriptions and sculpture. Abandoned in the Classic Maya collapse; Pakal's tomb was found in 1952.
evidence: Alberto Lhuillier and Pakal's Tomb (historicalmx.org): 'Sources agree that Alberto Ruz Lhuillier opened the chamber in 1952 (exact date given as June 15, 1952, in the Temple of the Inscriptions at Palenque).'
fix: The 1952 tomb discovery and Pakal's identity are confirmed. I did not find a page for the abandonment in the Classic Maya collapse.

text: Bosporus: The narrow strait at Constantinople between the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara. It made Constantinople rich and nearly impregnable for 1,500 years, and it is still Russia's only warm-water exit.
evidence: Wikipedia, Bosporus: 'Its historic Golden Horn is an estuary off the main strait that historically acted as a moat to protect Constantinople from attack.'
fix: The strait's location is correct. I found no source for 'nearly impregnable for 1,500 years', and the city fell in 1204 and 1453. I also found no source that the strait is Russia's only warm-water exit. Soften or remove both.

text: Stadium Quarter (Delos): Neighborhood surrounding the stadium in the settlement of Delos, constructed during the Hellenistic period.
evidence: Stadium Quarter (Pleiades) (pleiades.stoa.org): 'Neighborhood surrounding the stadium in the settlement of Delos, constructed during the Hellenistic period.'

text: Styra: Styra was an ancient port city located in the southwestern part of Euboea that possessed also an inland acropolis (on the modern peak of Hagios Nikolaos), extensive quarries, and a series of large stone structures known today as drakospita (dragon's houses).
evidence: Styra (Pleiades) (pleiades.stoa.org): 'Styra was an ancient port city located in the southwestern part of Euboea that possessed also an inland acropolis (on the modern peak of Hagios Nikolaos), extensive quarries, and a series of large stone structures known today as drakospita (dragon's houses).'

text: Zakros: A Minoan site in eastern Crete and the location of a Bronze Age palatial center.
evidence: Wikipedia, Zakros: 'Zakros is a Minoan archaeological site on the eastern coast of Crete in Lasithi, Greece. It is regarded as one of the six Minoan palaces.'

text: ?, 1663 CE: Toya eruption, 1663.
evidence: Usu Volcano (volcanodiscovery.com): '1663 (16 Aug - 5 Sep+-4 d)'
fix: The 1663 eruption was of Usu, a stratovolcano on the rim of the 110,000-year-old Toya caldera. It was not a Toya caldera eruption. Rename it 'Usu eruption, 1663'.

text: ?, 2013 CE: 2013 India–Pakistan border incidents.
evidence: Wikipedia, 2013 India–Pakistan border skirmishes: 'worst bout of fighting in the region in nearly 10 years'

text: ?, 1909 CE: Tragic Week.
evidence: Wikipedia, Tragic Week (Spain): 'The Tragic Week (Setmana Tràgica) was a series of violent confrontations in Barcelona and other Catalan cities from 25 July to 2 August 1909'

text: ?, 1555 CE: Battle of Miyajima.
evidence: Wikipedia, Battle of Miyajima: 'Wikipedia dates the battle to 16 October 1555 and calls it a decisive Mōri clan victory over Sue Harukata.'

text: ?, 908 CE: Battle of Eisenach.
evidence: Wikipedia, Battle of Eisenach: 'The battle took place on 3 August 908 at Eisenach in Thuringia. Hungarian forces won a decisive victory over an East Frankish army.'

text: ?, 1356 CE: Siege of Breteuil.
evidence: Wikipedia, Siege of Breteuil: 'The siege of Breteuil was a French siege of a Norman town held by supporters of Charles II of Navarre, lasting from April to about 20 August 1356.'

text: ?, 1477 CE: Siege of Krujë.
evidence: Wikipedia, Siege of Krujë (1477–1478): 'Wikipedia dates the siege from spring 1477 to 16 June 1478, with Ottoman forces under Evrenosoğlu Ahmed Bey blockading the fortress.'
fix: Optionally give the span as 1477–1478, since the siege ended with the Ottoman capture in June 1478.

text: Vyshny Volochyok had about 13,554 people in 1859 CE.
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source gave an 1859 figure. The 1860 Britannica gives 8,340 for 1856, which is a different year and a lower number. Check the 1859 Russian Empire statistical compilations.

text: Costa Rica had about 150,227 people in 1874 CE.
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source gave 150,227 for 1874. The 1864 census recorded 120,499 and the 1883 census recorded 182,073, so an 1874 figure of about 150,000 fits between them. That makes it plausible, but it is an interpolation and not confirmed.

text: Equatorial Guinea had about 102,371 people in 1892 CE.
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source gave an 1892 figure. The only snippet found says Rio Muni's population was officially put at a little over 100,000, but its year was cut off, so it can't be tied to 1892. Check colonial-era Spanish Guinea sources.

text: Vyazma had about 15,600 people in 1897 CE.
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source found with the 1897 population of the town of Vyazma. The page gives only the uyezd total, 105,502, which is not the town figure.

text: Nizhniy Novgorod had about 45,000 people in 1400 CE.
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source found with a population for Nizhny Novgorod around 1400. The earliest figure found is 40,742 in 1867, so 45,000 in 1400 looks implausible.

text: Sultanate of Harar lasted from 1547 CE to 1578 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Emirate of Harar: ''Ali ibn Da'ud reigned from 1647 to 1671 and founded a dynasty that governed Harar and its surrounding areas.'
fix: The Harar state (Emirate of Harar) began in 1647 and lasted until the Ethiopian conquest in 1887, not 1547–1578. The Adal Sultanate moved its capital to Harar in 1520 and was succeeded by the Imamate of Aussa, listed as established in 1577.

text: Kingdom of Lunda lasted from 1709 CE to 1889 CE.
evidence: Lunda Empire (newworldencyclopedia.org): 'New World Encyclopedia gives the kingdom's span as c. 1665-1887.'
fix: Change the dates to about 1665–1887. The Wikipedia infobox gives the 17th century to 1887. The search results gave no support for 1709 or 1889.

text: Maitraka Dynasty peaked around 656 CE at about 0.303531 million km².
evidence: No source settled it.
fix: No source found for a peak area of 0.303531 million km² around 656 CE. The dynasty ruled Gujarat from about 475 to 776 CE and came under Harsha's overlordship in the mid-7th century.

text: Lesotho peaked around 1973 CE at about 0.031741 million km².
evidence: Wikipedia, Lesotho: 'Area • Total: 30,355 km2 (11,720 sq mi) (137th)'
fix: The area is 30,355 km², or 0.030355 million km², not 0.031741 million. I found nothing on 1973 as a peak year.
